title: Workplace injury / OSHA documentation - case-derived candidate
summary: A 2026 OSHA Form 301 case provides direct evidence that OSHA injury/illness incident documentation is used in at least one RTEC workplace-injury record flow. Reporting, workers' compensation, medical, OSHA log, supervisor, return-to-work and retention steps remain to be established.

claims.claim: RTEC retained an OSHA Form 301 injury/illness incident report in at least one 2026 workplace-injury case.
The OSHA Form 301 likely participates in a broader workplace-injury and/or workers' compensation process, but the complete workflow cannot be established from one case.

controls: Medical and injury case details remain restricted and must not be generalized into the global knowledge layer.
unresolved_questions: Who completes OSHA Form 301 and when?
How does Form 301 relate to OSHA 300/300A logs?
What workers' compensation forms and carrier notifications are required?
What reporting deadlines and supervisor notifications apply?
How are medical restrictions/return-to-work handled and segregated from general personnel files?
